title: Microsoft Learning Zone: Minecraft Education connected lessons with Build Challenges and class reports
summary: The roadmap facts and documented product controls are supported, but the briefing overstates what licence assignment establishes about in-game permissions. Microsoft documents that faculty licences confer the teacher role with elevated permissions, not that licence type determines everyone who can run teacher controls.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the connected-lessons feature itself.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Learning Zone" "Minecraft" connected lessons default rollout licensing student reports Build Challenges'; opened both cited deployment pages. Results describe the surrounding products and unrelated Minecraft training, not connected lessons.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Whether connected lessons require licensing beyond the documented Learning Zone and Minecraft Education requirements is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Learning Zone" "Minecraft" "license"'; opened Deploy Microsoft Learning Zone and Get and deploy Minecraft Education; read Minecraft Education service-description search excerpts. No connected-lessons-specific entitlement or additional licence found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explained whether every student assigned a connected lesson needs a paid Minecraft Education licence or can use trial logins.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Learning Zone" "Minecraft" "license"' and '"Learning Zone" "Minecraft" connected lessons default rollout licensing student reports Build Challenges'; opened both deployment pages. Minecraft trial rules are documented, but their connected-lesson handling is not.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Which Minecraft activity data feeds connected-lesson reports is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Learning Zone" "Minecraft" "data"' and '"Learning Zone" Minecraft Build Challenges lesson generation 10 slides licensing data reports'; opened the Learning Zone and Minecraft deployment pages. No connected-lessons report payload or activity-data specification found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Device limit for generation; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not established whether Build Challenge matching counts as lesson generation for the published device limits.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Learning Zone" Minecraft Build Challenges lesson generation 10 slides licensing data reports'; opened Deploy Microsoft Learning Zone. It defines lesson-generation device limits but does not describe Build Challenge matching or classify it as generation.

claims.claim: Connected-lessons rollout mechanics and changes to existing product behaviour on arrival are not published.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Learning Zone" "Minecraft" rollout default admin switch'; read the roadmap and both deployment pages. The roadmap supplies the target, platforms, cloud and phase but no rollout mechanism or replacement of existing behaviour.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes tools for creating and launching lessons, not a change to autonomous actions.
claims.quote: AI-powered tools that match curriculum goals to Build Challenges, blend lessons with project-based learning, launch directly from Learning Zone

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects included Learning Zone access and user-assigned Minecraft Education entitlement, without asserting a new integration licence.
claims.quote: Add the relevant Minecraft Education, A1 for device or A3/A5 license if it is not assigned already

claims.claim: Licence type decides who can run in-game teacher controls.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Minecraft Education teacher role faculty license elevated permissions operator student teacher controls'; 'Minecraft Education teacher permissions students operator world host teacher license'; read Get and deploy Minecraft Education. No exclusive permission rule found.
claims.fix: Remove ', so licence type decides who can run in-game teacher controls'. Retain: 'Assigning a faculty Minecraft Education licence gives the user the teacher role in Minecraft Education with elevated permissions.' The cited deployment page supports that narrower statement.
